question:
D2 — Review all 7 design dimensions, or focus on the biggest gaps?
Project/branch/task: main branch; design review of PLAN.md (User Dashboard Page), rated 4/10 on design completeness.
ELI10: The plan says what the server does and lists which states must exist, but not what a person actually sees when they land after login. The biggest holes are page hierarchy (which of the three panels matters most), what each loading/empty/error state looks like, and accessibility/responsive detail. I'll generate visual mockups next, then work through the review passes and fix the plan pass by pass.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Skipping passes leaves gaps an engineer fills with defaults ("No items found.", stacked cards on mobile); running all 7 costs more questions but lands a complete plan.
Recommendation: A because AI makes the complete review cheap and the plan is thin on every visual dimension, not just three.
Completeness: A=10/10, B=6/10
Pros / cons:
A) All 7 passes (recommended)
  ✅ Every dimension gets rated and fixed: hierarchy, states, journey, slop risk, tokens, a11y, open decisions
  ✅ Produces a plan an implementer can build without guessing (human: ~half day / CC: ~30 min of questions)
  ❌ More AskUserQuestion stops, roughly one per finding across seven passes
B) Focus on hierarchy, states, and a11y/responsive only
  ✅ Fastest path to fixing the three worst gaps
  ✅ Fewer interruptions if you already have taste decisions made elsewhere
  ❌ Slop risk, token specificity and the decision register go unrated, and there is no DESIGN.md to fall back on
Net: thoroughness now versus fewer stops now and more guesses at build time.

options.label: All 7 passes (recommended)
options.description: ✅ Every dimension rated and fixed; plan buildable without guessing. ✅ Full coverage in ~30 min of CC questions. ❌ More decision stops, about one per finding.

options.label: Focus on hierarchy, states, a11y
options.description: ✅ Fastest path to the three worst gaps. ✅ Fewer interruptions. ❌ Slop, tokens and decision register unrated with no DESIGN.md fallback.
